statements: For all a,a',b,b' in G, if aN = a'N and bN = b'N, then abN = a'b'N.

replacements.claim: Suppose aN = a'N and bN = b'N. Then a^{-1}a' and b^{-1}b' lie in N. Since N is normal, b^{-1}(a^{-1}a')b lies in N; multiplying it by b^{-1}b' shows that (ab)^{-1}(a'b') = b^{-1}(a^{-1}a')b(b^{-1}b') lies in N. Hence abN = a'b'N, so coset multiplication is well-defined.
replacements.self_contained_claim: For all a,a',b,b' in G, if aN = a'N and bN = b'N, then a^{-1}a', b^{-1}b' are in N, and normality gives (ab)^{-1}(a'b') = b^{-1}(a^{-1}a')b(b^{-1}b') in N; therefore abN = a'b'N and coset multiplication is well-defined.
